title: Vertebral compression fracture treatment
description: A vertebral compression fracture treatment is an outpatient procedure where your surgeon uses either vertebroplasty or kyphoplasty to repair a broken vertebra caused by osteoporosis, cancer, or trauma. These fractures cause severe pain and loss of height. Your surgeon injects cement into the fractured vertebra to stabilize it and relieve pain. The procedure takes 30-60 minutes per vertebra, and you may go home the same day. You can return to light activities within a day or two, though you should avoid strenuous activity for several weeks. Pain relief is often immediate. Your surgeon may perform vertebroplasty, where cement is injected into the fracture, or kyphoplasty, where a balloon is inflated to restore vertebral height before cementing. This type of procedure can be performed various ways, including vertebroplasty and kyphoplasty, and the cost may vary depending on the specific approach or service provided.
